questions.question: For boundary-inclusive rectangle containment, which comparison is appropriate?
options: B) px > maxX and py > maxY
D) minX <= px <= maxX and minY <= py <= maxY
questions.explanation: Both coordinate intervals must contain the point, including their endpoints.

questions.question: For [1,5] x [2,6], where is point (1,4)?
questions.explanation: Its x equals the left bound and its y lies between the vertical bounds.

questions.question: After handling boundary points, an eastward ray with five proper crossings indicates what?
After handling boundary points, an eastward ray with four crossings indicates what?
What endpoint convention does the lecture use for crossing counts?
options: B) Include upper y, exclude lower y without changing anything else
D) Include lower y, exclude upper y
questions.explanation: The half-open rule prevents double counting at shared vertices.

questions.question: How should horizontal edges be treated?
options: A) Delete them before all processing
C) Count them twice for every query
D) Check boundary membership but skip them in the parity count
questions.explanation: They can contain the query point even though they do not contribute ordinary ray crossings.

questions.question: Why test whether p is on an edge before applying parity?
options: A) It guarantees an odd crossing count
B) Boundary membership is a separate contract decision
D) It changes every polygon into a rectangle
questions.explanation: The general lecture algorithm includes boundary points; parity handles points off the boundary.

questions.question: For an eligible edge, which intersection is counted by the eastward ray?
options: A) An intersection with xHit > px
C) Every intersection regardless of x
questions.explanation: An eastward ray contains points strictly to the right after the boundary case is removed.

questions.question: Edge (2,0) to (6,4) intersects y=1 at which x?
For edge (2,0) to (6,4), does query (4,1) count its intersection?
options: A) No; the hit at x=3 is west of the query
B) Yes; every nonhorizontal edge counts
C) No; the edge is horizontal
D) Yes; the query y is positive
questions.explanation: Eligibility in y alone is insufficient; the hit must be east of p.

questions.question: A nonhorizontal edge spans y=1 through y=5. Which query y is excluded by the half-open rule?
questions.explanation: The upper endpoint is excluded, while the lower endpoint is included.

questions.question: For a polygon with n edges, a full ray-casting query takes what time?
How can the same routine implement strict-interior containment?
options: C) Return false when p is on any boundary edge, then use parity otherwise
questions.explanation: The boundary decision changes; the off-boundary parity result does not.

questions.question: How should an exact point-on-segment test be implemented?
options: A) Only a positive dot product
B) Collinearity plus inclusive endpoint bounds
C) Only equal distances to both endpoints
D) Only equality of x coordinates
questions.explanation: A point can be collinear but beyond an endpoint.

questions.question: What happens to parity at a local y-extremum vertex under the half-open rule?
options: C) Incident edges contribute zero or two crossings, so tangency does not toggle parity
D) Every extremum contributes exactly one
questions.explanation: The rule handles tangential contacts consistently.

questions.question: For rectangle polygon (0,0),(4,0),(4,3),(0,3), how many eastward crossings does p=(1,1) have?
questions.explanation: Only the right edge is east of the query.

questions.question: For the same rectangle, p=(5,1) has how many eastward crossings?
questions.explanation: All boundary intersections at that y lie west of the query.

questions.question: Why should you read the method contract before classifying a boundary point?
options: A) Parity alone always distinguishes all three classes
B) Boundary points never occur in geometry
C) The lecture's inclusive algorithm and interior-only exercise use different boundary conventions
D) Every Java method must exclude boundaries
questions.explanation: Specify whether the required result includes or excludes boundary membership.
